decisions.reason: The same-message MODIFY already removes the obsolete multi-board orientation, interboard-alignment, cable-access, and board-order constraints. The remaining connector type, orientation, ESP32 placement, and dimensional attributes are not necessarily canceled by the source decision.
Acceptance of the proposed connector-edge distribution does not change the integrated board's cost goal, component-tier preference, connector-reduction goal, or sourcing exception.
The same-message MODIFY already records that no separate power board exists in the single-board design and removes its obsolete mechanical-layout attributes.
The same-message MODIFY already records that no separate sensor board exists in the single-board design and removes its obsolete mechanical-layout attributes.
The source permits flexible connector placement but does not alter the required light-sensor port's quantity, connector type, interface, or purpose.
The source relies on and reaffirms the already-established single-board architecture without changing its consolidation or functionality-preservation requirements.
Connector-edge placement does not change the requirement that all connectors use through-hole assembly.
The source concerns physical connector distribution and does not alter the backlight circuit, electrical topology, supply options, control behavior, or component values.
The connector-placement approval does not change the ESP32 breakout pin-header pitch.
The source does not change charging behavior, required voltage rails, battery-efficiency goals, or the selected AXP2101 power-management component.
Connector-edge distribution has no necessary effect on current-measurement capability or the conditional omission of a separate INA device.
The source addresses where connectors may be placed on the integrated board, not the USB-C connector's data-line capability or sourceability requirements.
